criterion_notes.c1: Examines rural household access to drinking-water sources (indoor tap, outdoor tap, improved water source, public water network connection) and sanitation services (public sanitation network connection or septic system).
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain wording, the study evaluates a statutory property-rights and administrative reform (Legislative Decree 25902 establishing the Special Rural Cadastre and Land Titling Project, PETT). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, formal land tenure/property title and removal of registration/documentation barriers ('documentation or tenure requirements' and administrative hurdles) are directly analyzed as rule-type legal/institutional determinants governing household water and sanitation network connections by utilities/municipalities and households.
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative quasi-experimental empirical study analyzing survey data from 3,204 rural households (3,182 regression observations) from the 2004 Land Titling Special Project Survey using marginal effects, a modified difference-in-differences design exploiting phased spatial roll-out and pre-program title status, and propensity score matching.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports multiple household-level service access outcomes: use of an improved water source, river water, or tanker truck/vendor; toilet/sanitation access (public sanitation connection or septic system); realization of a public water network connection or public sanitation network connection within the prior 5 years; household connection investment/financing; and monthly water payment indicators.
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (3,204 rural households in coastal, highlands and jungle regions of Peru; n = 3,182 in regressions; household unit of analysis), exposure (formal property title / PETT land-titling program reach interacted with no prior title), outcomes (water and sanitation source/connection and investment indicators), and study design (cross-sectional survey with quasi-experimental modified difference-in-differences and propensity score matching) are all clearly specified.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in English.

raw_response.exposure: Formal land titling / property rights reform via Peru's Special Rural Cadastre and Land Titling Project (PETT, enacted under Legislative Decree 25902), measured both by household PETT title vs. other title vs. no title and by the quasi-experimental interaction of village-level PETT program implementation with household lack of pre-PETT property title.
raw_response.outcome: Household water and sanitation access: use of an improved water source (indoor tap, outdoor tap, fountain, well/spring), river water, or tanker truck/vendor; access to toilet/sanitation (public sanitation connection or septic system); realization of a public water network connection or public sanitation network connection within the 5 years prior to survey; household connection expenditures/financing source; and monthly water payment indicators.
raw_response.population_and_sample: Rural households across Peru's coastal, highlands and jungle regions from the 2004 Land Titling Special Project Survey (total N = 3,204 households; regression sample n = 3,182 households; unit of analysis: household).
raw_response.rationale: This English-language empirical paper meets all inclusion criteria under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Using data on 3,204 rural Peruvian households and a quasi-experimental modified difference-in-differences design, it tests whether formal land titling and removal of bureaucratic title-registration hurdles under Peru's PETT program (tenure/documentation status) affect household access to improved water sources, public water network connections, and public sanitation/septic connections, as well as utility versus household connection investment channels. Statistical effect sizes are also extractable for quantitative synthesis.
raw_response.study_design: Quasi-experimental study (modified difference-in-differences exploiting spatial roll-out of the PETT land-titling program and pre-program household title status, supplemented with marginal effects regressions and difference-in-differences with propensity score matching) using cross-sectional household survey data.
